key_facts: BACKGROUND — PAROLE RETALIATION PATTERN: Plaintiff Brendan Ngehsi Newanforbi (BNN) has been subject to a documented pattern of parole officer retaliation in response to litigation activity. On January 12, 2026, BNN filed a First Amended Complaint in Newanforbi v. Andrew Derrick et al., Case No. 2:26-cv-00004-DJC-JDP (E.D. Cal.), a §1983 action against his then-assigned parole agent Andrew Derrick. On or about January 26, 2026 — approximately 14 days after the Derrick FAC — BNN's parole file was transferred to Long Moua, a colleague of Derrick at the same parole unit. The temporal proximity between the Derrick lawsuit and the file transfer to Moua establishes the first link in the retaliatory chain. CASOMB COMPLAINT & TELEHEALTH DIRECTIVE: On February 23, 2026, BNN submitted a formal complaint to the California Sex Offender Management Board (CASOMB) against HOPE Psychotherapy, Inc. (BNN's court-ordered treatment provider), documenting that HOPE had failed to create, review, and sign a treatment plan with BNN and had not discussed treatment progress — both legally required elements of sex offender treatment. On February 26, 2026, CASOMB investigator Dr. Kirsten Mason emailed BNN (at 3:09 PM) to confirm these specific deficiencies; BNN responded the same day affirming neither had occurred. On February 27, 2026, BNN requested a telehealth accommodation from CDCR. On March 18, 2026 at 1:36 PM, Agent Moua called BNN (incoming call, 55 seconds, from +1(510)227-9994 — see IMG_7328.png) and directed BNN to stop attending in-person group sessions at the HOPE facility at 5403 N Pershing Ave, Stockton, and instead attend telehealth sessions with Pam Akins beginning March 31, 2026. At 2:07 PM that same day, BNN texted Kelly Phaysaleum at HOPE to confirm no further in-person attendance was required; Kelly's response at 2:14 PM was 'Please contact your agent.' — confirming that HOPE had not been formally notified of the telehealth transition. FABRICATED VIOLATION — MARCH 31, 2026: On March 25, 2026 at 3:24 PM, Moua texted BNN: 'Starts 3/31/26 / Telehealth for HOPE / Tuesdays/Thursdays / 9AM-1030AM / Call 617-675-4444.' At 3:29 PM, BNN replied: 'Is there an Access Code for this conference call I should be aware of?' Moua never responded to this question. On March 31, 2026 at 9:01 AM — the morning of the first scheduled telehealth session — BNN texted Moua: 'Agent Moua, please provide me with the Google pin needed to enter the call.' Moua again did not respond. BNN could not enter the session without the access code and was therefore unable to attend. On April 1, 2026 at 9:35 AM, Moua texted BNN: 'Come to the office.' At the office, Moua questioned BNN about the missed telehealth session. BNN stated he had attempted to obtain the access code needed to enter the conference call. Moua asserted he had provided the code — a claim directly contradicted by the contemporaneous text message record, which shows no access code was ever transmitted. Moua then stated affirmatively that he would submit this as a violation — 'failure to attend treatment' — into the parole system. This fabricated violation became the manufactured pretext for the retaliatory transfer that followed. MACY'S EMPLOYMENT: On May 28, 2026, BNN started employment as Captain Selling & Support at Macy's, Stockton Sherwood store, earning $21.50/hour. By the time of the June 29, 2026 retaliatory transfer, BNN was working a regular schedule at Macy's (schedule printed July 2, 2026 at 3:16 PM shows active shifts through at least July 18, 2026 — see My Schedule.pdf). The Macy's position represents BNN's primary active employment at the time of the retaliatory transfer. SECOND LAWSUIT — CDCR RETALIATION ACCELERATES: On June 11, 2026, BNN filed Newanforbi v. CDCR, et al., Case No. STK-CV-UPI-2026-0005417 (San Joaquin Superior Court, Judge Jayne Lee, Dept. 10C; CMC December 9, 2026 at 8:30 AM). On June 22, 2026, defendants CDCR and Dodd were served with that lawsuit. On June 29, 2026 — exactly 18 days after filing and 7 days after service — Moua called BNN and directed him to report to the Stockton parole office for a urine sample. After BNN provided the UA, Moua announced that BNN's file was being transferred to the Santa Clara Parole GPS Unit. Moua's cited reason: 'Too many violations.' The March 31 fabricated telehealth violation — manufactured by Moua himself by withholding the access code then submitting BNN's inability to attend as willful non-compliance — was among the violations cited. The 18-day interval between the CDCR lawsuit service and the transfer order (Jun. 22 → Jun. 29, 2026) establishes the strongest possible causal nexus for First Amendment retaliation; the temporal proximity is direct evidence of retaliatory motive. EMPLOYMENT DESTRUCTION: On July 2, 2026, BNN reported to Agent Brown at the Santa Clara GPS Unit — the same day BNN's last Macy's shift occurred (Macy's is located in Stockton, approximately 60+ miles from Santa Clara). BNN notified Agent Brown of his Macy's position by text, sending his work schedule and the Macy's job offer letter; BNN asked Agent Brown 'Do I have your permission to keep going to work while I transition to Santa Clara sir?' (see IMG_7325.png, IMG_7326.png). No documented permission was granted. From July 5–8, 2026, Macy's manager Lety Villarreal sent multiple texts notifying BNN of missed shifts (July 5 and July 7); BNN initiated a medical Leave of Absence on July 7–8, 2026, with a preferred return date of August 12, 2026 (see Macy's LOA texts). BNN has not worked at Macy's since July 2, 2026. The retaliatory transfer to Santa Clara effectively made it impossible for BNN to continue the Stockton employment — the transfer destroyed BNN's income stream with no legitimate administrative basis. BNN was earning approximately $860/week gross ($21.50 × 37–40 hours/week). RESIGNATION — JULY 31, 2026: the LOA never converted back to active employment. On Friday, July 31, 2026, Lety texted BNN at 10:36 AM checking in ('We spoke yesterday about you coming in today 10a-7pm?'); at 10:42 AM BNN replied that he needed to resign effective immediately, explaining that his parole supervision had been abruptly transferred to Santa Clara County, where he now resides, and that the commute back to Stockton was 'impossible for me right now'; BNN thanked Macy's for the opportunity and apologized. Lety responded at 10:45 AM, 'Oh no ok, yeah that's a little far from here to commute. It was a pleasure working with you. Thank you for letting me know. Good luck take care.' BNN replied 'Thank you Ms. Lety, likewise' at 11:02 AM. This exchange converts the Macy's LOA (an open, potentially reversible status) into a completed resignation — a discrete, dated, and irreversible job loss that BNN attributed in writing, contemporaneously, to the Santa Clara parole transfer, directly and without third-party inference. CDCR FORM 1502-DR: On November 14, 2025, Moua authored a CDCR Form 1502-DR (Discharge Review Report); the report was reviewed and electronically signed by Noguchi (Badge #7284) as Moua's direct supervisor. Sacramento County Superior Court subsequently questioned why CDCR undertook this discharge review at all, creating a judicial record of suspicious administrative conduct predating the January 2026 Derrick FAC. NOGUCHI AS CO-DEFENDANT IN DERRICK FAC: Gary Noguchi was named as a co-defendant in the Newanforbi v. Andrew Derrick et al. FAC (Case 2:26-cv-00004-DJC-JDP, E.D. Cal.) — establishing that Noguchi had actual and constructive knowledge of BNN's litigation activity before he approved the retaliatory transfer. This is a critical supervisory liability fact: Noguchi co-authored the 1502-DR with Moua and is Moua's direct supervisor, making him personally aware of the retaliatory risk. GOVERNMENT CLAIMS ACT EXHAUSTION (Gov. Code §945.4): On July 18, 2026, BNN filed a Government Claim with the California Government Claims Program ($25 fee processed), satisfying the exhaustion requirement for Bane Act and IIED state law claims. The 45-day response period is anticipated to expire September 1, 2026 without written notice of rejection; the claim will then be deemed rejected by operation of law under Gov. Code §912.4(c), triggering the 2-year limitations period under Gov. Code §945.6(a)(2). The complaint is prepared for filing September 16, 2026 — after the anticipated deemed rejection and well within limitations. HOMELESSNESS: BNN became homeless on July 2, 2026, the date he first reported to the Santa Clara GPS Unit following the retaliatory transfer, and remains homeless as of this writing, residing at 1455 Cat Tail Drive, Stockton, CA 95204. The retaliatory transfer directly caused BNN's housing instability by uprooting him from his established Stockton support network. SEX OFFENDER REGISTRATION UNDER DURESS: On July 6, 2026, BNN completed mandatory sex offender re-registration at the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office, 55 W. Younger Avenue, San Jose, California, at 4:00 PM by appointment. BNN was required to register within the statutory period as a transient, scheduled to re-register August 5, 2026 per the 30-day transient requirement. Failure to timely register would have triggered BNN's third strike under California's Three Strikes Law, resulting in twenty-five years to life in state prison. Completing this legally compelled registration during a period of active housing displacement and employment destruction — caused directly by Moua's retaliatory transfer — constitutes a severe predicate act for IIED. SERVICE OF PROCESS ON MOUA MATTER DEFENDANTS: Gary Noguchi was served on July 7, 2026 at 11:46 AM (1 attempt; $50 waived; SUB OKAY per CountySuite/Teleosoft portal — see IMG_7327.png). Joseelyn Rojo was served on July 14, 2026 at 10:20 AM (4 attempts; $50 waived; SUB OKAY per CountySuite/Teleosoft portal — see IMG_7327.png). Both were served under an earlier complaint draft naming them directly; the operative Complaint v9 deliberately narrows the pleading to Moua and DOES 1-10 only, a confirmed strategic choice reserving Noguchi and Rojo for potential later DOE amendment rather than an oversight. Service on Moua himself pending. JOB OFFER DOCUMENT: The Macy's offer letter (Job Offer-Selling and Support Captain, Stockton Sherwood - Full Time.pdf) confirms: title Captain Selling & Support, base pay $21.50/hr, start date May 28, 2026, Stockton Sherwood store.
